description: Consumed fuel over the event trace
comment: Each total is measured from the start of evaluating the program expression: the program's entry region (the closure creation), the invocation event, and every region entry and event charge the invocation produces. Derivations are spelled out per case; see docs/runtime/execution-limits.md for the cost law.

cases.description: square: one invocation, one entry region, one builtin event
cases.comment: program entry region 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 2 (two $var) + mul builtin 1 = 5.

cases.description: branching charges only the selected arm: $then
cases.comment: program entry 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 2 + gt builtin 1 + selected arm region 1 = 6.

cases.description: branching charges only the selected arm: $else, same total by symmetric constants
size-metered builtin inputs and value production
cases.comment: program entry 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 2 + strcat builtin (base 1 + rest sizes 5 + 5) + produced string 10 = 25.

cases.description: string sizes are Unicode code points
cases.comment: program entry 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 1 + upper builtin (base 1 + 3 code points) + produced string 3 = 10.

cases.description: a strict $let binding charges once in its containing region; rereads add nothing
cases.comment: program entry 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 5 (the $let node, the binding's $var and literal, and the two $var reads in $in) + add builtin 1 + mul builtin 1 = 9. The binding folds into the body region; each later $var read is an already-counted node, not a new charge.

cases.description: aggregation meters its array input; a scalar result produces no value charge
cases.comment: program entry 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 1 + sum builtin (base 1 + input length 4) = 8.

cases.description: callback traversal charges one event per callback call
cases.comment: program entry 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 2 ($fn node + literal 3) + range builtin 1 + produced range array 3 + map builtin 1 + three neg builtin events 3 + produced map array 3 = 15.

cases.description: annotations do not change consumed fuel
cases.comment: The annotated form of the square program: $type and $returns payloads contribute zero to region constants, so the total is identical to the bare form's 5 (program entry 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 2 + mul builtin 1).

cases.description: a supplied argument never enters the default region
cases.comment: program entry 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 2 + mul builtin 1 = 5. The default-force event attaches only to an omitted parameter; the default expression's region contributes nothing here.

cases.description: an omitted parameter's default region is entered at the binding's first read
cases.comment: program entry 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 2 + default region 2 (the add call's two literals) + add builtin 1 + mul builtin 1 = 8. The default-force event fires once, at the first $var read; the second read is an already-evaluated binding and adds nothing.

cases.description: an omitted parameter that is never read never enters its default region
cases.comment: program entry 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 1 (the literal) = 3. Whether and when a default is first read is value-determined, so the un-read default charges nothing.

cases.description: a lowered field default evaluates at bind time: the miss fires arm selection even though the binding is never read
cases.comment: program entry 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 4 (the $let node, the $get node, the $var target, and the literal in $in) + $else arm region 2 + add builtin 1 = 9. The projection is a strict $let binding, so the absent field enters the arm region when the binding evaluates, not at a read — contrast the positional $default above, whose region an un-read binding never enters. A pattern field never fires default force.

cases.description: a hit fires no event: the $else arm region is not entered
cases.comment: program entry 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 2 (the $get node and the $var target) = 4. The read stays in the containing region.

cases.description: a miss enters the $else arm region by arm selection
cases.comment: program entry 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 2 + arm region 1 = 5.

cases.description: a deciding $and operand ends the charge: the further operand's region is never entered
cases.comment: program entry 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 1 (the first operand's $var) = 3. The boolean validation of the evaluated operand is region work, not an event; the second operand is neither evaluated nor charged.

cases.description: continuing into a further $and operand enters its region by arm selection
cases.comment: program entry 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 1 + second-operand region 1 = 4.

cases.description: closure creation charges its record entry in the containing region and fires no event
cases.comment: program entry 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 4 (the $let node, the function literal, its one record entry for a, and the argument literal) + f invocation 1 + f body entry region 2 (two $var) + add builtin 1 = 10. Applying the locally created value is an ordinary invocation; no re-entry charge applies to a value created in this evaluation.

cases.description: applying a hydrated function value charges re-entry 1; its record's cost was paid at creation
cases.comment: program entry 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 1 (the argument literal) + re-entry 1 + f invocation 1 + f body entry region 2 (two $var) + add builtin 1 = 8. The function value arrives as input, so entering it charges 1 for the value itself; its capture record was charged where the value was produced, and fuel does not cross that boundary.

cases.description: a closure created per callback invocation charges its record entry per iteration
cases.comment: program entry 1 + invocation 1 + body entry region 2 (the callback literal, which captures nothing, and the $var) + map builtin 1 + per element 9 (callback invocation 1 + callback body region 4: the $let node, the inner literal, its one record entry for x, and the argument literal + inner invocation 1 + inner body region 2 + add builtin 1) x 2 elements + produced map array 2 = 25. Each element re-enters the callback's body region, so the record entry is charged once per iteration.

cases.description: exhaustion is checked at event points: the size-metered builtin event exceeds the budget
cases.comment: Charges before the strcat event total 4; the event's 11 exceeds the remaining budget of 6.
